nodes.summary: Three points $P$, $Q$, $R$ of the Euclidean plane form an equilateral triple when, writing $d$ for the Euclidean distance, $d(P, Q) = d(Q, R)$ and $d(Q, R) = d(R, P)$. Coincident points are allowed, so $P = Q = R$ qualifies.
nodes.title: Equilateral triple of points

nodes.summary: Points $A$, $B$, $C$, $P$, $Q$, $R$ of the Euclidean plane form a Morley configuration when $A$, $B$, $C$ are not collinear, each of $P$, $Q$, $R$ lies in the closed triangle $ABC$, and, writing $\angle XYZ \in [0, \pi]$ for the unoriented angle at $Y$, $0 < \angle CAR = \angle RAP = \angle PAB$ and $3 \angle PAB = \angle CAB$; $0 < \angle ABP = \angle PBQ = \angle QBC$ and $3 \angle QBC = \angle ABC$;…
nodes.title: Morley configuration

nodes.summary: A point $X$ of the Euclidean plane lies in the triangle with vertices $A$, $B$, $C$ when $X$ belongs to the convex hull of $\{A, B, C\}$, the closed triangle $ABC$ (a segment or a point when $A$, $B$, $C$ are collinear).
nodes.title: Point in a closed triangle

nodes.summary: If points $A$, $B$, $C$, $P$, $Q$, $R$ of the Euclidean plane form a Morley configuration, so that $ABC$ is a nondegenerate triangle and $P$, $Q$, $R$ are the intersections of its adjacent angle trisectors, then $P$, $Q$, $R$ form an equilateral triple: writing $d$ for the Euclidean distance, $d(P, Q) = d(Q, R)$ and $d(Q, R) = d(R, P)$.
nodes.title: Morley's trisector theorem

nodes.summary: The Euclidean plane $\mathbb{R}^2$ with its standard Euclidean distance.
nodes.title: Euclidean plane for Morley's theorem

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
